content: Zolpidem is a medication prescribed to treat insomnia, which is characterized by difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep. It belongs to a class of drugs known as sedative-hypnotics and works by slowing brain activity to facilitate sleep. Zolpidem is available in two forms: a standard tablet and an extended-release tablet, both of which are taken orally. It is typically taken as needed at bedtime. For optimal effectiveness, it should not be taken with or immediately after a meal, as this may delay its onset of action. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take zolpidem exactly as directed. You will likely feel very sleepy shortly after taking it and may remain drowsy for some time. Plan to go to bed immediately after taking zolpidem and ensure you can stay in bed for 7–8 hours. Do not take zolpidem if you cannot commit to staying asleep for this duration, as waking up too soon may result in memory problems. Swallow extended-release tablets whole; do not split, chew, or crush them. Your sleep issues should improve within 7–10 days of starting zolpidem. If your symptoms do not improve or worsen during this time, contact your doctor. Zolpidem is generally intended for short-term use. Prolonged use (beyond two weeks) may reduce its effectiveness and increase the risk of dependence. Discuss the risks of long-term use with your doctor. Do not take larger doses, take it more frequently, or use it for longer than prescribed. If you have been taking zolpidem for more than two weeks, do not stop it abruptly without consulting your doctor, as this may lead to withdrawal symptoms such as seizures, tremors, muscle cramps, vomiting, sweating, or difficulty sleeping. These symptoms are usually temporary and improve within a few nights. Zolpidem may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking zolpidem, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to zolpidem or any other medications. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are taking or plan to take. Certain medications, such as antidepressants, anxiety medications, sedatives, and others, may interact with zolpidem, requiring dose adjustments or careful monitoring for side effects. Inform your doctor if you consume large amounts of alcohol, use street drugs, or have a history of substance misuse. Additionally, disclose any history of depression, sleep apnea, breathing problems, myasthenia gravis, or liver or kidney disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Zolpidem should not be used during breastfeeding. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking zolpidem. Zolpidem may cause daytime drowsiness and increase the risk of falls. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Do not consume alcohol while taking zolpidem, as it can exacerbate side effects. Some individuals taking zolpidem have engaged in activities such as driving, eating, or making phone calls while partially asleep and later had no memory of these actions. If this occurs, contact your doctor immediately. Zolpidem may cause unexpected changes in mental health, such as aggression, hallucinations, memory problems, or worsening depression. Notify your doctor immediately if you experience any of these symptoms or if you have thoughts of self-harm. Ensure your family is aware of these potential symptoms so they can seek help on your behalf if necessary. Unless otherwise directed by your doctor, continue your normal diet while taking zolpidem. If you forget to take a dose at bedtime and are unable to fall asleep, you may take zolpidem if you can remain in bed for 7–8 hours afterward. Do not take it if you are not ready to sleep immediately. Zolpidem may cause mild side effects, including drowsiness, dizziness, headache, gastrointestinal issues, muscle or joint pain, and unusual dreams. If these symptoms persist or worsen, inform your doctor. Serious side effects, such as allergic reactions, difficulty breathing, chest pain, or vision problems, require immediate medical attention. Report any unusual problems to your doctor. Serious side effects can also be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch program. Store zolpidem in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from heat and moisture. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, consulting your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact a poison control center at 1-800-222-1222 or call 911 if the individual has collapsed or is not breathing. Symptoms of overdose may include extreme drowsiness, slowed breathing, or coma. Keep all appointments with your doctor and do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
